12-# CUDA Optimization Worker (tree variant)
13-
14:You are a frontier CUDA researcher and optimization expert running one **brief** the `/autocuda:optimize-tree` manager wrote for you. You **exhaustively explore the brief**: edit, build, validate, benchmark, profile, commit, and log every trial, then return to the manager. You do not analyze the run, judge whether an idea has merit, decide what to try next, or declare an idea dead, impossible, exhausted, or a dead end — those are the manager's calls. You report what you tried and what you measured.
15-
16-## Arguments
17-
18:The manager passes these to you in the launch prompt — read them off it:
19-
20:- `brief-id=<K>` — the brief's global id, supplied by the manager. It names your branch, worktree, and log; pass it to every `autocuda ...` call you make for this brief.
21:- `tag=<tag>` — the shared run tag the manager chose at startup. Every brief in the run uses the same tag.
22:- `data-dir=<path>` — absolute path to the shared autocuda data directory, given by the manager from its `autocuda init manager` capture. Forward this verbatim to every `autocuda ...` invocation you make.
23-
24-The **active set** is whatever the run's reference row measured: the exact `(benchmark, axis-value-point)` combinations whose cells in the baseline row of `<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-reference-log.csv` carry a number rather than `N/A`. The set is frozen for the run. Every trial must exercise every benchmark in it on every axis value the baseline used — same benchmarks, same axes, same values. You do not restrict, expand, or substitute. See *Constraints § Active set is locked by the baseline*.
25-
26-## Layout
27-
28:You operate inside `<data-dir>/worktrees/optimize-<tag>-brief-<brief-id>/`, the worktree `autocuda init brief` creates for this brief. The brief gets its own branch (`autocuda/optimize/<tag>/brief-<brief-id>`) created and checked out by `autocuda init brief`. Your trial rows go to `<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-brief-<brief-id>-log.csv` (the brief log); you read the run's reference row from `<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-reference-log.csv` and read but do not write the manager log (`<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-manager-log.csv`). Profiles you produce land under `<data-dir>/profiles/<tag>/` and end in the trial's commit SHA so the next brief can find them by glob.
29-
30-## Setup
31-
32-1. **Read `<data-dir>/layout.md` and `<data-dir>/environment.md`.** From `layout.md`: the project structure, editable files, build commands, validation commands, every benchmark (and its axes/aggregation), the cross-benchmark aggregation policy, and logging. From `environment.md`: the per-step timeouts and the profiler invocations for this machine.
--
36-5. Run the trial loop.
37-
38-## Reading your brief
39-
40:Run `autocuda init brief --data-dir <data-dir> --tag <tag> --brief-id <brief-id>`. The CLI reads the brief the manager wrote under this id, creates and checks out the brief's branch off its first parent commit inside the brief's worktree, and prints labelled lines:
41-
42-- `WORKTREE="<absolute-path>"` — `cd` here before your first trial.
43-- `BRANCH="<name>"` — the brief's branch the CLI created and checked out for you.
44-- `BRIEF="<objective>"` — pursue this for the duration of this brief; if a trial would not advance the objective, you're off-brief.
45-- `BRIEF_KIND="macro"|"micro"|"combine"|"simplify"` — the brief's classification. `macro` = big structural changes; `micro` = narrow tuning; `combine` = integrate two or more prior trials (the branch starts at the first parent; integrating the rest is part of the brief); `simplify` = shrink the `diff_lines` benchmark without regressing the performance benchmarks (see *Methodology § Simplify briefs*). Only an `autocuda:simplify` run writes `simplify` briefs.
46-- `BRIEF_ID="<K>"` — this brief's global id; pass it as `--brief-id` to every later `autocuda log optimize-tree` call.
47-- `PARENT_COMMITS="<sha>[;<sha>...]"` — semicolon-separated parent SHAs. One for macro / micro; two or more for combine.
48:- `MODE="fresh"|"resume"` — `resume` when re-entering this brief after a stop (prior trials are on the branch HEAD); `fresh` otherwise.
49-- `PARENT_METRIC_<bench>="<value>"` — one line per benchmark, the first parent's metrics.
50-- `PARENT_PROFILE="<path>[,<path>...]"` — comma-separated absolute paths to the parents' profile captures (typically one `.nsys-rep` and / or one `.ncu-rep` per parent). Omitted when no profile file matches.
51-
52-`cd` into `$WORKTREE`. Read the parent profile(s) listed in `$PARENT_PROFILE` before deciding what to edit — the parent commit was already profiled by whoever produced it, so re-profiling now would be redundant. Then research the brief: read code in the worktree, docs in `references/`, prior commits and rows from this run on other briefs' branches and brief logs, and the open web for relevant CUDA / library / kernel material. Investing in research up front makes your work informed instead of speculative.
--
72-   Use `--status succeeded` for any trial that ran cleanly. Use `build_error` / `validation_error` / `runtime_error` for failures. Pass `--metric <bench>=<value>` for **every benchmark** declared in the schema; the only allowed `<bench>=N/A` cells are baseline-`N/A` cells and failure-row cells (see *Constraints § Active set is locked by the baseline*). The CLI rejects rows that omit a benchmark.
73-8. **Profile** per *Methodology § Profiling*. Save outputs as `<data-dir>/profiles/<tag>/brief-<brief-id>-trial-<#>-<commit-sha>.{nsys,ncu}-rep`, using the full SHA reported by the log command, so the next brief that forks off the commit can find them.
74-9. Go to step 1.
75-
76:When you hand the brief back to the manager, **profile the final trial** if you didn't already (so the parent of any follow-up brief has a profile to read), then record that you are stopping and your return message:
77-```
78:autocuda log optimize-tree stop \
79-    --data-dir <data-dir> --tag <tag> --brief-id <brief-id> \
80:    --description "<return-message>"
81-```
82-
83:The return message reports what you tried and what you measured — best score reached, what each edit did to the metric — and presses the manager to keep the work going. Name concrete directions still open under this objective: knobs you didn't sweep, structural variants you didn't reach, directions you uncovered but didn't pursue. The manager decides what is worth pursuing; your job is to surface the openings, not to close them. See *Operating rules § Speak in measured terms*.
84-
85:The manager may push you to keep going on this same brief: it sends a continuation message and you resume the loop above on the same branch and log. When it does, log a fresh `brief_start` only if you had already logged a `brief_stop` and are re-entering, so each pass gets its own start/stop pair. A new objective is a different brief with a different id, started by a freshly-spawned worker, not this one.
86-
87-## Methodology
88-
89-### Keep going; a regression isn't the end of an idea
--
91-Within the brief's objective, keep working the design space. A trial that doesn't improve the metric is fine — commit it anyway: a refactor or restructuring that regresses but sets up a bigger change is part of the work. **Sometimes you have to take a step back to take a step forward.** A first cut at an idea usually regresses; that is not a reason to drop the idea — keep working it rather than handing it back after one bad number.
92-
93-### Build the idea, don't pre-judge it
94-
95:Implement the brief in the live code and let the measured number be the verdict — don't argue on paper that it's too hard or won't pay off, or hand back a *disproof* you reached without building. A negative result from a built, benchmarked, committed kernel is a measurement; one reasoned to without is a guess. You execute and measure; the manager judges whether the direction has merit. Surface what you measured and what's still open in your return message — never a verdict that the idea is done.
96-
97-### Structural changes
98-
99-**Prioritize structural changes** — algorithms, access patterns, redundant work — over micro-optimization and parameter tuning. Be bold and pursue big and complex ideas, even if they require lots of code changes. Try it now; don't defer work or try a simpler change first. Take on the hard thing regardless of how long or difficult it looks.
--
117-The parent profile from `$PARENT_PROFILE` covers trial 1, so the only trials you must profile are:
118-
119-- trial 1 *if* `$PARENT_PROFILE` is empty (no parent capture was found);
120-- at least every 5th trial after that;
121:- the final trial before `brief_stop`, so the next brief that branches off your work has a profile to read.
122-
123-Profile more aggressively when the brief is making non-obvious progress and the next edit's direction depends on freshly-measured bottlenecks. Reach for `ncu` once you know which kernel to attack — it explains *why* a kernel is slow where `nsys` only locates the time. Read the profile before the next edit; it tells you what to try next within the brief. For profiler selection, invocation, and the output filename convention, see `references/profilers.md`.
124-
125-### Aggregating across axes
--
155-Every change you explore goes in the editable files and is measured by the real benchmark. Never put kernel code — or a benchmark of it — anywhere else: a standalone script, a proxy, an out-of-tree microbenchmark, or a component you mean to port later runs under different conditions than the live path, so its numbers don't compare to the baseline and aren't a result.
156-
157-### Commit what you measured
158-
159:Commit the live code you actually ran, with its real metric — **even a regression**, which the manager simply doesn't pick as a parent. Don't gate a change off, comment it out, or leave dead alternatives behind, and don't return a brief reverted to its parent: that discards the measured result the branch exists to capture.
160-
161-### Active set is locked by the baseline
162-
163:Every trial must produce a metric for every `(benchmark, axis-value-point)` whose cell in the manager's baseline row carries a number, on exactly those axis values. No `N/A` cells outside of those that were `N/A` in the baseline. No restricting axes, no expanding axes, no swapping axis values.
164-
165-Read the active set off the baseline row in `<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-reference-log.csv` at setup time: the benchmarks whose baseline cells carry a number are in the active set; the axis values the baseline measured are the axis values you measure. A succeeded row carries a number for every active-set benchmark; `<bench>=N/A` is allowed only where the baseline cell was already `N/A` or where the row's status is a failure.
166-
167-### Stay on-brief
168-
169:If you find yourself wanting to advance an objective outside the current brief, **don't**. Stay on the brief; surface any new hypotheses to the manager in your return message and let them write a fresh brief. The manager's diversity check across the briefs in flight is what prevents wasted parallel work.
170-
171-### No peeking outside this run
172-
173:Reading other briefs' logs and commits within this run's tag is fine — that's how you learn what other briefs have tried in related parts of the tree. **Never** read anything from outside it, even when it would answer your question directly: prior logs from other tags, prior analysis notes, prior `autocuda/optimize/<other-tag>/*` branches, and any summary of past results are off-limits. Build your own evidence in this run; a finding that leaned on a past conclusion is not real and taints the run. When you catch yourself reaching outside the tag, stop and surface the question to the manager instead.
174-
175-## Concurrency
176-
177-Every build / validate / benchmark / profile invocation **MUST** go through `autocuda run`, which coordinates the fleet through per-GPU file locks on `<data-dir>/.gpu-<g>.lock`. Two subcommands matter:
--
180-- **`autocuda run exclusive --data-dir <data-dir> -- <cmd>`** — used for **validate**, **benchmark**, and **profile** (`nsys` / `ncu`). Claims any free GPU, pins `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to it, and takes its exclusive lock with no resource limits; blocks every build and any benchmark on that same GPU, while benchmarks on other GPUs run concurrently. No `--agent-id` — the GPU is chosen dynamically, so a build never waits on a busy GPU while another is free.
181-
182-Direct invocations (`./bench`, `cmake --build build`, `nsys ...`) bypass the locks and the GPU pin, producing noisy / wrong measurements as soon as another brief is running — always wrap.
183-
184:**No polling shells.** Don't write `until [ -f <file> ]; do sleep N; done` or `while true; do … sleep N; done` loops to work around the harness's blocked-sleep guard. `autocuda run` is synchronous — `slice` / `exclusive` return when the wrapped command exits, no waiting needed on your side.
185-
186:**Stay on your own brief-id.** Every `autocuda log optimize-tree` call from this worker uses the `--brief-id` the manager assigned. Never write a row under another brief's id. Briefs are written by the manager only — workers cannot write to the manager log.
187-
188-## Operating rules
189-
190:**Stay on-brief.** Re-read the constraint in the *Stay on-brief* section above. The manager owns objective and parent selection; you own trial choices within the brief.
191-
192-**Try hard things.** You can and should pursue ideas that require big and complex code changes.
193-
194:**Execute; don't judge.** You build and measure. You do not decide whether the idea works, whether the approach is right, or what to try next — those are the manager's. Report your measurements and the openings you see; let the manager steer.
195-
196:**Speak in measured terms.** Never call an idea impossible, exhausted, converged, fully optimized, a dead end, the best possible, or settle anything definitively — neither in the loop nor in your return message. State what you measured and what remains open. Your return message presses the manager to keep going and names concrete unexplored directions; it never concludes the work is finished.
197-
198:**NEVER STOP between trials.** Inside a brief's loop, don't pause to ask the human if you should continue, don't ask "is this a good stopping point?", don't schedule wakeups. Keep running trials, then return cleanly to the manager. Between briefs is the only place control returns to the manager.

# autocuda contributor guide for AI coding agents

This file is read by Claude Code (via `CLAUDE.md` symlink resolution) and other AGENTS.md-aware harnesses (Codex, Aider, etc.). The conventions below apply to every change, regardless of which agent wrote it.

## Scope is the operator's call, not yours

Agents do not get to decide what work belongs in a PR. The operator's instruction is the scope; the answer is "ship a complete fix".

- **Never push back on an instruction because it's "too big".** When the operator describes a multi-file change, a sweep across skills, or a refactor with broad blast radius, the answer is "ok, doing it" — not "this is a lot, want to split into multiple PRs?", not "this expands #N's scope considerably, are you sure?", not a numbered list of clarifying questions. Plan the work, do the work, surface unknowns inside the work (in commit messages or the PR body), not in a pre-flight Q&A. Operator scope decisions are final on first instruction.
- **Never ask "if you say do it, I'll go" or its variants.** If you've reached the point of describing what you'd do in detail and inviting the operator to greenlight it, you have already wasted a turn — start with the work instead. The operator's original instruction is the greenlight. Phrases like "want me to land this in #N or as a follow-up?", "let me know if anything looks off", "if anything looks off, say so" are forbidden when used as a confirmation gate before action; they are fine *after* the work is done as a sanity check.
- **Do all the work the instruction implies.** If the operator says "rename skill X to Y", that includes every README / plugin.json / marketplace.json reference, not just the skill directory rename. If the operator says "add CLI flag F to subcommand S", that includes the `Namespaces` block, the `--help` text, the test, and every skill that should now use the flag instead of inventing the value itself. A change shipped without its consequences is incomplete, not "scoped".

Specifically banned, in PR bodies, commit messages, issue comments, design docs, and code comments:

- *Out of scope* / *out-of-scope* (any capitalization), as a section header or inline qualifier.
- *Follow-up PR* / *follow-up issue*, used to defer work that the current change should have included.
- *Left for later* / *leaving X for a separate PR* / *deferred to a future change*.
- *Future work* sections in design docs that list things the current PR should have done.
- *Deliberately not addressing X here* / *not in scope* — the operator decides scope, not the agent.

If a change is *truly* independent — an orthogonal cleanup the agent noticed in passing, with its own diff and its own test path — it belongs in its own PR opened in parallel, not in a "scope note" appended to the current one. The bar for "independent" is high: if dropping the orthogonal change makes the current PR's test plan honest about what's tested vs. broken, it isn't independent.

## No backwards compatibility

autocuda is pre-1.0 and has no external users running off its schemas, CSV layouts, branch names, or CLI surface. We do not preserve old shapes across renames. When the design changes, the codebase changes — there is no migration window, no deprecation period, and no compatibility shim layer.

Concretely, in any PR that renames or restructures a thing:

- **No legacy aliases.** When a column / flag / status / argument / file path is renamed, the old name disappears. Don't add `row.get("agent_id") or row.get("worker_id")` fallbacks, don't keep a `--deprecated-alias` next to the new flag, don't accept both old and new header names in CSV readers.
- **No version branching for the migration period.** If a schema or on-disk format changes, the new version is what the codebase reads and writes. Don't keep a "version 1 fallback path" alive on the assumption old runs need to keep working — they don't.
- **No "graceful warning" for the old shape.** A caller passing the old shape gets an error, not a warning that papers over the rename. The agent reading the error then fixes the call site.
- **No deprecation comments.** Removed code stays removed. `# Deprecated, will be removed in vX` and `# kept for backward compat` are forbidden — those just defer the cleanup that should have landed in the same diff.
- **No re-exports of moved symbols.** When a function moves modules, callers update.
- **Tests update too.** A test fixture that constructs the old shape is part of the rename, not exempt from it. The whole test suite reflects current code.

The only exception is genuinely external interfaces we don't own: the GitHub API, kernel `flock` semantics, `nsys` / `ncu` output formats, the on-disk format of git objects. Those we accept as we find them. Everything inside `autocuda/` — log schemas, CSV column headers, branch namespaces, CLI flags, skill argument names, profile filename conventions — is fair game to change without an upgrade path.

If a rename is genuinely too large to land in one PR, that means the PR scope is wrong (split it into independently-renamable units), not that the codebase needs a transitional layer.

## Style

### Issues

- Close issues from the PR via `Closes #N.` in the PR body — don't manually close before merge. Multiple issues each need their own keyword: `Closes #1, #2.` only closes #1 and treats the bare `#2` as a mention, so write `Closes #1. Closes #2.` (or `Closes #1, closes #2.`) to pick up both.

### Documentation

When a change touches user-visible surface, update the docs that describe it in the **same PR** — don't leave the docs as a follow-up:

- **A new or renamed skill** → update the top-level `README.md` (the `## How it works` skill list, the `### Artifacts` and `### Branches` trees if applicable, and the `## Project structure` block listing the skill directory), `plugins/autocuda/README.md`, `plugins/autocuda/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s description, `plugins/autocuda/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`'s description, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`'s description, and `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` if the marketplace metadata changes.
- **A new or renamed sub-agent** (a definition under `plugins/autocuda/agents/`, e.g. `optimize-tree-worker` that the `optimize-tree` manager spawns) → update the same `README.md` surfaces (the `## How it works` entry for the manager skill that spawns it and the `## Project structure` `agents/` listing), `plugins/autocuda/README.md`, and every manager skill that spawns it by `name` or by `agents/<name>.md` path. The agent's `name:` frontmatter is the `subagent_type` the manager launches — rename it and the manager's launch call must follow.
- **A new or renamed CLI subcommand or flag** → update the module docstring at the top of `plugins/autocuda/lib/autocuda_cli.py` (the `Namespaces` block) and the `help=` text on every affected argparse parser. The `--help` output is the agent's primary discovery surface — keep it accurate.
- **A change to the on-disk layout** (new file kind under `autocuda/`, new branch namespace, new schema) → update the README's `### Artifacts` and / or `### Branches` trees so the layout is auditable at a glance.
- **A change to the contributor flow** (new pre-commit / pre-push hook, a new required setup step, a new style rule) → update this file (`AGENTS.md`) so the next agent picks the rule up automatically.

The rule is: if `git diff main` shows a user-visible change, `git diff main -- README.md plugins/autocuda/README.md AGENTS.md` should show a doc update on the same line of work. If it doesn't, the PR is incomplete.

### Avoid documenting history

**Documenting history in source is strictly forbidden.** Code and design documents describe what *is*, not what *was*. Git contains the history; PR descriptions explain the change; issue threads carry the discussion. Don't duplicate that into the tree.

If a sentence's meaning depends on the reader knowing what this file or the surrounding code used to say, it's history — delete it. The test is mechanical: cover the rest of the document, read the sentence on its own, ask *"does this still make sense to someone who has never seen the prior version?"* If no, the sentence is history.

- No `# previously this …` / `# changed from … to …` / `# this used to be a …` comments. Same ban on the prose equivalents — *"a previous version of this"*, *"this used to"*, *"until recently"*, *"we removed"*, *"the old behaviour was"*.
- No "we tried X but switched to Y because Z" prose. State Y. The reason it isn't X belongs in the PR that made the switch.
- No motivation-by-history — don't justify the present rule by what it replaced (*"this is strict because the old version got abused"*). The rule is its own justification; design pressure that shaped it goes in the PR description, not the doc.
- No `(see #NN)` / `(#NN fixed this)` parentheticals embedded in docstrings, help text, or skill prose — those are PR-description material. Cross-references *to currently-open* issues for known-bug behaviour are fine; cross-references to *closed* issues that motivated a rule are not.
- No bug-incident write-ups embedded in source. The post-mortem belongs in the PR that fixed the bug.
- No incident counts or audit statistics. *"Polling shells were the worst offender in the harness audit that filed this rule — 25 occurrences across 6 worker JSONLs in one run"* is history dressed up as evidence; the rule stands or falls on its own statement. State the rule, period.
- No "this rule was filed because …" / "the audit that produced this rule found …" / "we found N instances of …" framing. These are PR-description sentences that wandered into the source.
- Removed code stays removed. Don't comment it out, don't `# (removed in #NN)` it.

A reader walking into the file cold should see only what's true now. If they need the history, `git log` and `git blame` are one keystroke away. If a rule needs evidence to justify it, that evidence belongs in the PR description, the linked issue, or both — never in the source tree.

### Skill prose: be concise, defer detail

The top-level SKILL.md for each skill is loaded into the agent's context every time the skill runs. Token cost compounds across the iterative skills (`optimize-simple`, `optimize-tree`, `simplify`, `combine`, `explore-brief`) because they re-read the skill on every iteration (see the *Re-read* rule in each loop). `explore-brief` in particular is loaded into every worker the `optimize-tree` manager spawns. Budget tokens accordingly.

- **Lead with what the agent must do**, in the imperative. State the rule, then stop. No motivation paragraphs, no "this is here because", no "in the past we tried X".
- **Cap subsections.** Each `###` subsection under `## Optimization strategy` / `## Constraints` / `## Operating rules` is at most ~5 short paragraphs. If it grows past that, the load-bearing rule is buried — extract.
- **Detail goes in `references/<topic>.md`**, not in SKILL.md. The skill prose names the topic, points at the reference, and moves on. Examples of progressive disclosure already in the tree: `references/profilers.md` (full `nsys` / `ncu` invocation form), `references/libraries.md` (the CUDA library catalogue). When a new long-form explanation would otherwise land in a SKILL.md, write a new reference file instead and cite it.
- **No examples in skill prose unless the example is load-bearing.** A reader who already knows what an `nsys` invocation looks like doesn't need to see one in SKILL.md; they need to know *which* invocation form to use, and the reference file has that.
- **Cite, don't restate.** If a rule already lives in another skill or in `references/`, point at it. Two copies of the same rule drift apart and the reader gets both at double the token cost.
- **Use `name=value` for skill arguments.** In `argument-hint` and skill invocation prose, write skill arguments as `repo=<path>` / `agent-id=<N>`. Reserve `--flag` syntax for actual shell commands and CLI examples.

The check: open the diff for any SKILL.md change. If a paragraph could be replaced by *"see `references/<topic>.md`"* and the skill would still tell the agent what to do, replace it.

### Placeholder spelling in skill prose

Three placeholder styles appear in skill prose; mixing them within the same skill creates noise. The convention is:

- **Type/shape placeholders** — `<N>`, `<path>`, `<slug>`, `<value>`, `<name>` — describe the *shape* of a value the caller supplies. Use these in `argument-hint` and on first definition of an argument: `workers=<N>`, `data-dir=<path>`, `repo=<slug>|<path>`.
- **Argument-name placeholders** — `<tag>`, `<agent-id>`, `<data-dir>` — refer back to an argument by its noun. Use these in body prose once the argument has been introduced: *"every worker uses the same `<tag>`"*, *"the worker cds into `<data-dir>`"*.
- **Shell variables** — `$TAG`, `$DATA_DIR` — appear only inside fenced shell snippets, and only after a visible `NAME=...` capture step in the same skill (e.g. `eval "$(autocuda init manager --workers 3)"`).

Always backtick `<placeholder>` tokens in prose so they're never mistaken for HTML. Don't introduce a fresh placeholder name (`<id>`) when the argument's actual name (`agent-id`) is already in scope — refer back by the argument's name, not a paraphrase.

### Markdown style

- **No artificial line wrapping** in prose. One paragraph = one long line. Some older files in the tree still hard-wrap at ~80 chars; touching them is an opportunity to unwrap, but don't make a separate PR for it. New prose ships unwrapped.
- **ATX headings** (`# H1`, `## H2`, `### H3`) — never setext (`===` / `---` underlines).
- **Dash bullets** (`- foo`), not asterisks or plus.
- **Fenced code blocks** with a language tag where it's meaningful (` ```bash`, ` ```python`, ` ```text`). Plain ``` is fine for shell snippets without a clear language.
- **No trailing whitespace, no tabs.** The pre-commit `trailing-whitespace` and `mixed-line-ending` hooks enforce this.

### Pre-commit and pre-push hooks

The repo gates `git commit` and `git push` with mechanical checks. Install once per checkout:

```bash
pip install pre-commit       # or `uv tool install pre-commit`
pre-commit install --install-hooks
```

`pre-commit install` wires the hooks into `.git/hooks/`. After that, `git commit` runs the pre-commit stage (whitespace, ruff, shellcheck) and `git push` runs the pre-push stage (pytest). The same set of hooks runs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` against every PR.

Skip a single hook with `SKIP=<id> git commit` (e.g. `SKIP=ruff-format git commit`). Don't `--no-verify` — CI is the canonical gate and has none.

"""`autocuda status` — CSV-derived fleet state for the optimize-tree manager.

Reads `<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-manager-log.csv`, every
`<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-brief-<K>-log.csv`, and the reference log
`<data-dir>/<tag>-optimize-tree-reference-log.csv`, and emits a JSON
summary of activity, branchable trials, and measured progress that the
manager reads when a worker completes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

# How often `autocuda status` re-emits the verbatim optimize-tree SKILL.md
# on stderr (see `_maybe_emit_skill_reminder`). The manager loop calls
# `autocuda status` before every brief, so this gate turns "re-read the
# skill every 2 hours" from a self-policed instruction the manager can
# silently skip into a mechanical injection: the bytes land in context as
# a tool result, with nothing for the manager to attest to. Override with
# AUTOCUDA_SKILL_REMINDER_INTERVAL_SECONDS (0 disables the reminder).
_SKILL_REMINDER_DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 2 * 60 * 60
_SKILL_REMINDER_STAMP_NAME = ".status-skill-reminder"
_SKILL_REMINDER_BEGIN = "===AUTOCUDA_SKILL_REMINDER_BEGIN==="
_SKILL_REMINDER_END = "===AUTOCUDA_SKILL_REMINDER_END==="
_PROGRESS_LOOKBACK = timedelta(hours=1)
_PROGRESS_GAIN_THRESHOLD_PERCENT = 0.25
_PROGRESS_DWELL = timedelta(minutes=30)
_REALLOCATION_COOLDOWN = timedelta(hours=4)


class _TaggedSchemaCli:
    """Transparent CLI-module view whose legacy schema loader is tag-scoped.

    Keeping the tag selection at the status-command boundary lets the
    existing scoring helpers consume an immutable run schema without
    rewriting their control flow.  It also leaves independent status
    extensions free to replace those helpers without creating merge-only
    conflicts.
    """

    def __init__(self, module, tag: str):
        self._module = module
        self._tag = tag

    def __getattr__(self, name: str):
        return getattr(self._module, name)

    def load_schema(self, experiments_dir: Path) -> dict:
        return self._module.load_run_schema(experiments_dir, self._tag)


def _autocuda_cli_module(tag: str | None = None):
    import autocuda_cli  # noqa: PLC0415

    return autocuda_cli if tag is None else _TaggedSchemaCli(autocuda_cli, tag)


def _skill_reminder_interval_seconds() -> int:
    """Resolve the skill-reminder interval, honoring the env override.

    Returns the default 2h when unset; a non-negative override otherwise;
    0 disables the reminder. An unparseable or negative value falls back
    to the default rather than erroring out the status call.
    """
    raw = os.environ.get("AUTOCUDA_SKILL_REMINDER_INTERVAL_SECONDS")
    if raw is None or raw.strip() == "":
        return _SKILL_REMINDER_DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS
    try:
        value = int(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return _SKILL_REMINDER_DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS
    return value if value >= 0 else _SKILL_REMINDER_DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS


def _skill_md_path() -> Path:
    """Path to the optimize-tree SKILL.md shipped beside this CLI:
    `plugins/autocuda/lib/_manager.py` -> `plugins/autocuda/skills/...`.
    """
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "skills" / "optimize-tree" / "SKILL.md"


def _maybe_emit_skill_reminder(data_dir: Path, now: datetime) -> None:
    """Print the verbatim optimize-tree SKILL.md to stderr when at least
    one reminder interval has elapsed since the last emission.

    The reminder goes to **stderr** so stdout stays pure JSON for callers
    that pipe `autocuda status` into a parser; the manager reads both
    streams, so the skill text reaches its context regardless. A timestamp
    file under the data dir throttles emission. The first status call of a
    run (no stamp yet) always emits, re-seeding the manager with the rules
    at the start of the loop.

    Best-effort: a missing SKILL.md or an unwritable stamp file never
    fails the status call — the JSON summary is the contract, the reminder
    is an additive nudge.
    """
    interval = _skill_reminder_interval_seconds()
    if interval == 0:
        return

    stamp = data_dir / _SKILL_REMINDER_STAMP_NAME
    last: datetime | None = None
    try:
        last = _parse_log_timestamp(stamp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except OSError:
        last = None

    if last is not None and (now - last).total_seconds() < interval:
        return

    skill_path = _skill_md_path()
    try:
        text = skill_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return

    print(_SKILL_REMINDER_BEGIN, file=sys.stderr)
    print(
        "Periodic re-read of the optimize-tree skill (emitted by "
        "`autocuda status` because >= "
        f"{interval}s have elapsed since the last emission). The verbatim "
        "skill text follows; re-ground the management loop in it.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    print(file=sys.stderr)
    print(text, file=sys.stderr)
    print(_SKILL_REMINDER_END, file=sys.stderr)

    try:
        stamp.write_text(now.isoformat(), encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        pass


def _parse_log_timestamp(raw: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    """Parse a log timestamp as UTC.

    Empty or unparseable values return None. Offset-naive timestamps are
    interpreted as UTC so they can be compared with offset-aware log and
    wall-clock timestamps.
    """
    value = (raw or "").strip()
    if not value:
        return None
    if value.endswith("Z"):
        value = value[:-1] + "+00:00"
    try:
        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if ts.tzinfo is None:
        return ts.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def _numeric_text_key(value: str | None) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
    """Order numeric ids numerically, then other text lexicographically."""
    text = (value or "").strip()
    if text.isdigit():
        return (0, int(text), text)
    return (1, 0, text)


def _trial_order_key(row: dict) -> tuple:
    """Stable cross-file order independent of brief-log concatenation."""
    timestamp = _parse_log_timestamp(row.get("timestamp"))
    return (
        timestamp is None,
        timestamp or datetime.max.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc),
        _numeric_text_key(row.get("brief_id")),
        _numeric_text_key(row.get("trial")),
        (row.get("commit") or "").strip(),
        (row.get("description") or "").strip(),
    )
    `top_best` surfaces the top 10 branchable trials by default;
    `--top K` overrides that count, and the first entry is also exposed
    as `best_trial`. `global_best` includes the scoring reference at 1.0x,
    so a run whose trials all regress reports the reference as its record.

    `progress` exposes `stalled`, `trials_since_improvement`, and the
    cooldown-gated `reallocate` action signal. The stall detector requires the
    trailing one-hour exact-record gain to remain below 0.25% for 30 minutes.
    """
    m = _autocuda_cli_module(args.tag)
    err = m._validate_tag(args.tag)
    if err:
        print(f"error: {err}", file=sys.stderr)

    manager_log = m.manager_log_path(args.experiments, args.tag)
    brief_logs = m.all_brief_log_paths(args.experiments, args.tag)
    reference_log = m.reference_log_path(args.experiments, args.tag)
    if not manager_log.exists() and not brief_logs and not reference_log.exists():
        print(
            f"error: no optimize-tree logs found for tag {args.tag}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1

    manager_rows = _read_log_rows(manager_log) if manager_log.exists() else []
    brief_rows: list[dict] = []
    for path in brief_logs:
        brief_rows.extend(_read_log_rows(path))
    reference_rows = _read_log_rows(reference_log) if reference_log.exists() else []

    last_log_ts: datetime | None = None
    for r in manager_rows + brief_rows + reference_rows:
        t = _parse_log_timestamp(r.get("timestamp", ""))
        if t is None:
            continue
        if last_log_ts is None or t > last_log_ts:
            last_log_ts = t

    now = _resolve_now(args, last_log_ts)

    last_activity: dict[str, datetime] = {}
    last_activity_str: dict[str, str] = {}
    last_status: dict[str, str] = {}
    trial_count: dict[str, int] = {}
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()

    for r in brief_rows:
        bid = (r.get("brief_id") or "").strip()
        if not bid:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(bid)
        status = r.get("status", "") or ""
        ts = _parse_log_timestamp(r.get("timestamp"))
        if status not in m.BRIEF_LIFECYCLE_STATUSES and status not in m.REFERENCE_STATUSES:
            trial_count[bid] = trial_count.get(bid, 0) + 1
        if ts is not None:
            prev = last_activity.get(bid)
            if prev is None or ts > prev:
                last_activity[bid] = ts
                last_activity_str[bid] = r["timestamp"]
                last_status[bid] = status

    parent_commit_by_brief: dict[str, str] = {}
    for r in manager_rows:
        brief_id = (r.get("brief_id") or "").strip()
        if not brief_id:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(brief_id)
        parents_cell = (r.get("parent_commits") or "").strip()
        # Manager log carries `parent_commits` as a semicolon-separated
        # list (combine briefs name 2+ parents; macro / micro name
        # exactly one). For ranking and global-best lineage we only
        # need the primary parent — that's the merge base for combine
        # briefs and the sole parent for the rest.
        parent = parents_cell.split(m.PARENT_COMMITS_SEP, 1)[0].strip() if parents_cell else ""
        if parent:
            parent_commit_by_brief[brief_id] = parent

    brief_ids = sorted(seen_ids, key=lambda b: (int(b) if b.isdigit() else 1 << 62, b))

    per_brief: list[dict] = []
    for bid in brief_ids:
        last_ts = last_activity.get(bid)
        if last_ts is not None:
            minutes_since = (now - last_ts).total_seconds() / 60.0
            last_ts_str = last_activity_str.get(bid, last_ts.isoformat())
        else:
            minutes_since = None
            last_ts_str = None
        per_brief.append(
            {
                "brief_id": bid,
                "last_activity_ts": last_ts_str,
                "minutes_since_activity": (
                    round(minutes_since, 1) if minutes_since is not None else None
                ),
                "trial_count": trial_count.get(bid, 0),
                "last_status": last_status.get(bid),
            }
        )

    top_k = getattr(args, "top", 10)
    if top_k is None:
        top_k = 10
    if top_k < 0:
        print(f"error: --top must be >= 0, got {top_k}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    try:
        scoring_context = _scoring_context(args.experiments, args.tag, reference_rows, m)
        scoring_error = None
        ranked_trials = _compute_top_best(
            args.experiments,
            args.tag,
            brief_rows,
            reference_rows,
            parent_commit_by_brief,
            0,
            m,
            scoring_context,
        )
        optimized_reference = _optimized_reference(args.experiments, args.tag, reference_rows, m)
    except (KeyError, OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        scoring_error = str(exc)
        ranked_trials = []
        global_best = None
        progress = None
        progress_error = None
        optimized_reference = None
    else:
        try:
            global_best, progress = _compute_progress(
                args.experiments,
                args.tag,
                brief_rows,
                reference_rows,
                manager_rows,
                parent_commit_by_brief,
                m,
                scoring_context,
                now,
            )
            progress_error = None
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            progress_error = str(exc)
            progress = None
            global_best = _reference_best_entry(scoring_context)
            if ranked_trials and ranked_trials[0]["speedup"] > 1.0:
                global_best = ranked_trials[0]
    best_trial = ranked_trials[0] if ranked_trials else None
    top_best = ranked_trials if top_k == 0 else ranked_trials[:top_k]
    payload = {
        "tag": args.tag,
        "status_generated_at": now.isoformat(),
        "last_log_timestamp": last_log_ts.isoformat() if last_log_ts is not None else None,
        "per_brief": per_brief,
        "global_best": global_best,
        "best_trial": best_trial,
        "top_best": top_best,
        "progress": progress,
        "progress_error": progress_error,
        "scoring_error": scoring_error,
        "optimized_reference": optimized_reference,

    # Re-inject the verbatim skill on stderr at most once per interval, so
    # the manager loop is re-grounded mechanically rather than on the
    # manager's say-so. Uses the resolved `now` so `--as-of` snapshots are
    # deterministic. Best-effort; never blocks the JSON contract on stdout.
    _maybe_emit_skill_reminder(args.experiments, now)
    print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    return 0

def _trial_entry(
    tag: str,
    row: dict,
    metrics: dict[str, float],
    speedup: float,
    bench_names: list[str],
    parent_commit_by_brief: dict[str, str],
    rank: int,
) -> dict:
    brief = (row.get("brief_id") or "").strip()
    return {
        "rank": rank,
        "brief_id": brief or None,
        "trial": (row.get("trial") or "").strip() or None,
        "commit": (row.get("commit") or "").strip() or None,
        "branch": _branch_for_row(tag, row),
        "parent_commit": parent_commit_by_brief.get(brief) or None,
        "status": (row.get("status") or "").strip() or None,
        "timestamp": (row.get("timestamp") or "").strip() or None,
        "metrics": {name: metrics[name] for name in bench_names if name in metrics},
        "speedup": round(speedup, 6),
        "description": (row.get("description") or "").strip(),
    }


def _allocation_boundary(
    experiments_dir: Path,
    tag: str,
    manager_rows: list[dict],
    reference_rows: list[dict],
    cli_module,
) -> tuple[int, datetime]:
    """Return the first brief id and start time of the current allocation."""
    state = cli_module.load_allocation_state(experiments_dir, tag)
    if state is not None:
        started_at = _parse_log_timestamp(state["started_at"])
        if started_at is None:
            raise ValueError("allocation state has an invalid started_at timestamp")
        return state["first_brief_id"], started_at

    manager_times = [
        timestamp
        for row in manager_rows
        if (timestamp := _parse_log_timestamp(row.get("timestamp"))) is not None
    ]
    if manager_times:
        return 0, min(manager_times)

    reference_times = [
        timestamp
        for row in reference_rows
        if (timestamp := _parse_log_timestamp(row.get("timestamp"))) is not None
    ]
    if reference_times:
        return 0, min(reference_times)
    raise ValueError("cannot determine the current fleet allocation start")


def _brief_number(row: dict) -> int | None:
    value = (row.get("brief_id") or "").strip()
    return int(value) if value.isdigit() else None


def _record_at(records: list[tuple[datetime, float]], instant: datetime) -> float:
    """Forward-fill a monotone record series at `instant`."""
    value = records[0][1]
    for timestamp, candidate in records[1:]:
        if timestamp > instant:
            break
        value = candidate
    return value


def _compute_progress(
    experiments_dir: Path,
    tag: str,
    brief_rows: list[dict],
    reference_rows: list[dict],
    manager_rows: list[dict],
    parent_commit_by_brief: dict[str, str],
    cli_module,
    context: dict | None = None,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict | None, dict | None]:
    """Return the exact record and persistent allocation-local stall verdict.

    The exact global record still spans the whole run. Stall progress starts
    at the current allocation boundary and is reconstructed from record
    timestamps, so it is independent of status polling cadence.
    """
    if context is None:
        context = _scoring_context(experiments_dir, tag, reference_rows, cli_module)
    if now is None:
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    lifecycle = set(cli_module.BRIEF_LIFECYCLE_STATUSES) | set(cli_module.REFERENCE_STATUSES)
    attempts = [row for row in brief_rows if (row.get("status") or "") not in lifecycle]
    attempts.sort(key=_trial_order_key)
    first_brief_id, allocation_start = _allocation_boundary(
        experiments_dir, tag, manager_rows, reference_rows, cli_module
    )

    record_speedup = 1.0
    global_best = _reference_best_entry(context)
    boundary_speedup = 1.0
    current_attempts: list[tuple[datetime, dict]] = []
    current_successes: list[tuple[datetime, float]] = []

    for row in attempts:
        brief_id = _brief_number(row)
        timestamp = _parse_log_timestamp(row.get("timestamp"))
        scored = _score_trial(row, context, cli_module)
        if scored is not None:
            speedup, metrics = scored
            if speedup > record_speedup:
                record_speedup = speedup
                global_best = _trial_entry(
                    tag,
                    row,
                    metrics,
                    speedup,
                    context["bench_names"],
                    parent_commit_by_brief,
                    rank=1,
                )
            if brief_id is not None and brief_id < first_brief_id:
                boundary_speedup = max(boundary_speedup, speedup)
            elif (
                brief_id is not None
                and timestamp is not None
                and timestamp <= now
                and timestamp >= allocation_start
            ):
                current_successes.append((timestamp, speedup))
        if (
            brief_id is not None
            and brief_id >= first_brief_id
            and timestamp is not None
            and allocation_start <= timestamp <= now
        ):
            current_attempts.append((timestamp, row))

    records = [(allocation_start, boundary_speedup)]
    current_record = boundary_speedup
    for timestamp, speedup in sorted(current_successes):
        if speedup > current_record:
            current_record = speedup
            records.append((timestamp, speedup))

    last_material_improvement = allocation_start
    material_checkpoint = boundary_speedup
    ratio = 1.0 + _PROGRESS_GAIN_THRESHOLD_PERCENT / 100.0
    for timestamp, speedup in records[1:]:
        if speedup >= material_checkpoint * ratio:
            material_checkpoint = speedup
            last_material_improvement = timestamp
    trials_since_improvement = sum(
        timestamp > last_material_improvement for timestamp, _row in current_attempts
    )

    evaluation_start = allocation_start + _PROGRESS_LOOKBACK
    low_since: datetime | None = None
    if now >= evaluation_start:
        breakpoints = {evaluation_start, now}
        for timestamp, _speedup in records[1:]:
            if evaluation_start <= timestamp <= now:
                breakpoints.add(timestamp)
            expiry = timestamp + _PROGRESS_LOOKBACK
            if evaluation_start <= expiry <= now:
                breakpoints.add(expiry)
        for timestamp in sorted(breakpoints):
            current = _record_at(records, timestamp)
            previous = _record_at(records, timestamp - _PROGRESS_LOOKBACK)
            gain_percent = 100.0 * (current / previous - 1.0)
            if gain_percent < _PROGRESS_GAIN_THRESHOLD_PERCENT:
                if low_since is None:
                    low_since = timestamp
            else:
                low_since = None

    stalled = low_since is not None and now - low_since >= _PROGRESS_DWELL
    reallocate = stalled and now - allocation_start >= _REALLOCATION_COOLDOWN
    return global_best, {
        "stalled": stalled,
        "trials_since_improvement": trials_since_improvement,
        "reallocate": reallocate,
    }

    and speedup vs baseline (the perf floor the simplify search holds).

    Returns None for a non-simplify run (no `optimized` row in the

def _fan_out_width(data_dir: Path) -> tuple[int, str | None]:
    """Return `(N, error)` where N is the run's fan-out width — the
    `workers` count in `worker-limits.json`, i.e. the number of briefs the
    manager keeps in flight concurrently.
    """
    from _run import WORKER_LIMITS_FILE  # noqa: PLC0415

    limits = data_dir / WORKER_LIMITS_FILE
    if not limits.exists():
        return 0, f"{limits} does not exist; run `autocuda init manager` first"
    try:
        workers = int(json.loads(limits.read_text())["workers"])
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
        return 0, f"{limits} is malformed; re-run `autocuda init manager`"
    if workers <= 0:
        return 0, f"{limits} has a non-positive worker count"
    return workers, None


def _open_brief_count(data_dir: Path, tag: str) -> int:
    """Number of briefs currently in flight — briefs whose log holds an
    unmatched `brief_start` (no later `brief_stop`)."""
    m = _autocuda_cli_module()
    open_count = 0
    for path in m.all_brief_log_paths(data_dir, tag):
        last_lifecycle: str | None = None
        with path.open(newline="") as f:
            for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                status = (row.get("status") or "").strip()
                if status in ("brief_start", "brief_stop"):
                    last_lifecycle = status
        if last_lifecycle == "brief_start":
            open_count += 1
    return open_count


def _validate_brief_kind_balance(
    data_dir: Path,
    tag: str,
    brief_kind: str,
    min_share_by_kind: dict[str, float],
    *,
    remaining_slots_override: int | None = None,
    combine_exempt: bool = False,
) -> str | None:
    """Refuse a brief that makes any per-kind minimum-share quota
    unreachable.

    `min_share_by_kind` values are fractions in [0, 1]. The share is
    `count(kind) / count(all briefs ever written for this run)`, computed
    globally over the manager log with the candidate brief counted in. The
    reachability test asks whether the remaining slots in the current
    fan-out round — the fan-out width minus the briefs already in flight —
    can still cover any deficit.

    Round 1 is the special case: no briefs have been written. The combine
    quota does not bind round 1 (no succeeded trials exist to
    combine), so we only enforce macro / micro / simplify minima on
    round 1 and exempt combine. Once any brief is on record, every
    minimum binds normally.
    """
    m = _autocuda_cli_module()
    fan_out, err = _fan_out_width(data_dir)
    if err is not None:
        return err

    counts: dict[str, int] = dict.fromkeys(m.BRIEF_KINDS, 0)
    log = m.manager_log_path(data_dir, tag)
    total_written_before = 0
    if log.exists():
        with log.open(newline="") as f:
            for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                kind = (row.get("brief_kind") or "").strip()
                if kind in counts:
                    counts[kind] += 1
                    total_written_before += 1

    # Count the candidate brief.
    counts[brief_kind] = counts.get(brief_kind, 0) + 1
    total_briefs_after = total_written_before + 1

    # Slots still free in the current fan-out round: the fan-out width
    # minus the briefs already in flight (open brief logs), minus the
    # candidate brief itself (a fresh ephemeral worker fills one slot).
    remaining_slots = (
        max(0, remaining_slots_override)
        if remaining_slots_override is not None
        else max(0, fan_out - _open_brief_count(data_dir, tag) - 1)
    )

    # Forbid combine in round 1 — there are no succeeded trials on
    # disk yet, so a combine brief has nothing to merge.
    is_round_one = total_written_before == 0
    if brief_kind == "combine" and is_round_one:
        return (
            "--brief-kind=combine is not valid for the first round of briefs: "
            "no succeeded trials exist yet to combine. Use macro or micro "
            "for round 1 briefs."
        )
    if brief_kind == "combine" and combine_exempt:
        return (
            "--brief-kind=combine is not valid for a fresh fleet allocation"
        )

    for kind, min_share in min_share_by_kind.items():
        if min_share <= 0:
            continue
        if kind == "combine" and (is_round_one or combine_exempt):
            continue
        # Final-state denominator: total briefs once every remaining slot
        # in the round is filled. We can only commit on the candidate
        # brief here, so the lower bound on `count(kind)` is `counts[kind]`
        # plus any future briefs that *might* still be `kind`.
        # Reachability: `counts[kind] + remaining_slots`.
        final_total = total_briefs_after + remaining_slots
        if final_total <= 0:
            continue
        max_reachable = counts[kind] + remaining_slots
        max_share = max_reachable / final_total
        if max_share + 1e-9 < min_share:
            return (
                f"`{kind}` brief quota would be unreachable: candidate brief "
                f"plus {counts[kind] - (1 if brief_kind == kind else 0)} "
                f"prior `{kind}` row(s) leaves at most "
                f"{max_reachable} `{kind}` brief(s) across "
                f"{final_total} total — {max_share:.3f} < "
                f"{min_share:.3f} required (--min-{kind})"
            )
    return None

def cmd_log_optimize_tree_optimized(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Write a `status=optimized` row to the reference log.

    The optimized reference is the simplify run's second anchor: the
    optimized peak the simplify search forks off and must not regress
    below. Its metrics let the manager surface the perf floor (the
    optimized peak's speedup vs baseline) in `autocuda status`.
    """
    return _write_reference_row(args, "optimized")


def _search_root_commit(cli_module, data_dir: Path, tag: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Return the initial search parent: optimized for simplify, else baseline."""
    path = cli_module.reference_log_path(data_dir, tag)
    try:
        rows = _read_rows(path)
    except (OSError, csv.Error) as exc:
        return None, f"cannot read reference log {path}: {exc}"
    optimized = [row for row in rows if (row.get("status") or "").strip() == "optimized"]
    baseline = [row for row in rows if (row.get("status") or "").strip() == "baseline"]
    candidates = optimized or baseline
    expected = "optimized" if optimized else "baseline"
    if len(candidates) != 1:
        return None, f"reference log must contain exactly one {expected} row"
    commit = (candidates[0].get("commit") or "").strip()
    if not commit or commit.upper() == "N/A":
        return None, f"{expected} reference row is missing its commit"
    return commit, None


def cmd_log_optimize_tree_brief(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Append a brief row to the manager log.

    `brief_id` is auto-assigned as the next global id (the count of every
    brief row written for this run) and printed as `brief_id=<K>` so the
    manager knows which brief to spawn a worker for. `--parent-commit` is
    repeatable: macro / micro / simplify briefs name exactly one parent,
    combine briefs name two or more (the first is the merge base).
    """
    rc = _validate_optimize_tree_tag(args.tag)
    if rc is not None:
        return rc

    m = _autocuda_cli_module(args.tag)
    if args.brief_kind not in m.BRIEF_KINDS:
        print(
            f"error: invalid --brief-kind {args.brief_kind!r}; must be one of "
            f"{', '.join(m.BRIEF_KINDS)}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    parent_refs = [
        c.strip() for c in (getattr(args, "parent_commits", None) or []) if c and c.strip()
    ]
    if not parent_refs:
        print(
            "error: --parent-commit is required (repeatable for combine briefs)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    if args.brief_kind == "combine":
        if len(parent_refs) < 2:
            print(
                "error: --brief-kind=combine requires --parent-commit to be "
                "passed at least twice (the first parent is the merge base, "
                "the rest are merged onto it)",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

            return 2
        if allocation_state is not None and brief_id < (

        ):

            return 2

                file=sys.stderr,

            m, args.experiments, args.tag
        )
        if root_error is not None:
            print(f"error: {root_error}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        if args.brief_kind == "combine" or parent_commits != [search_root]:
            print(
                "error: the first replacement brief must be non-combine and "
                "start from the run's search-root commit",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
        timestamp = m.now_iso_utc()
        pending_allocation_state = {
            "allocation": (allocation_state["allocation"] if allocation_state else 0) + 1,
            "first_brief_id": brief_id,

    elif allocation_state is not None:

        return 2

    header = m.csv_header_from_schema(schema, "optimize-tree-manager")
    parent_commits_cell = m.PARENT_COMMITS_SEP.join(parent_commits)
    row = {
        "timestamp": (
            pending_allocation_state["started_at"]
            if pending_allocation_state is not None
            else m.now_iso_utc()
        ),
        "brief_id": str(brief_id),
        "parent_commits": parent_commits_cell,
        "brief_kind": args.brief_kind,
        "description": args.description,
    }
    log = m.manager_log_path(args.experiments, args.tag)
    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    _append_log_row(log, header, row)
    if pending_allocation_state is not None:
        m.write_allocation_state(args.experiments, args.tag, pending_allocation_state)
    print(f"brief_id={brief_id}")
    return 0

    plus the three failure statuses. The manager ranks `succeeded` rows

    promotion to improved/neutral/regressed. `trial` is

brief_id: str | int | None = None,

    """Resolve the log file for `(tag, skill[, brief_id])`.

    For `optimize-tree` the schema is split: the manager writes to

def allocation_state_path(experiments_dir: Path, tag: str) -> Path:
    """Internal boundary and cooldown state for the current fleet allocation."""
    return experiments_dir / f"{tag}-optimize-tree-allocation.json"


def load_allocation_state(experiments_dir: Path, tag: str) -> dict | None:
    """Return the current replacement-allocation boundary, if one exists."""
    path = allocation_state_path(experiments_dir, tag)
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as source:
        state = json.load(source)
    if not isinstance(state, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"allocation state at {path} must be a JSON object")
    allocation = state.get("allocation")
    first_brief_id = state.get("first_brief_id")
    started_at = state.get("started_at")
    if (
        isinstance(allocation, bool)
        or not isinstance(allocation, int)
        or allocation < 1
        or isinstance(first_brief_id, bool)
        or not isinstance(first_brief_id, int)
        or first_brief_id < 1
        or not isinstance(started_at, str)
        or not started_at.strip()
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"allocation state at {path} is malformed")
    return {
        "allocation": allocation,
        "first_brief_id": first_brief_id,
        "started_at": started_at,
    }


def write_allocation_state(experiments_dir: Path, tag: str, state: dict) -> None:
    """Atomically replace the current replacement-allocation boundary."""
    path = allocation_state_path(experiments_dir, tag)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{path.name}.", dir=path.parent)
    temporary_path = Path(temporary_name)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as target:
            json.dump(state, target, indent=2)
            target.write("\n")
            target.flush()
            os.fsync(target.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary_path, path)
    finally:
        temporary_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

def _seed_round_one_succeeded_briefs(tmp_path: Path, tag: str = "2026-01-01-00-00-00") -> None:
    """Write two macro briefs (so the run isn't in round 1) plus
    matching `succeeded` trial rows on each worker, so a follow-up
    `combine` brief can be tested without the round-1 short-circuit
    rejecting it.
    """
    _setup_schema(tmp_path)
    _write_worker_limits(tmp_path, n=3)
    _run(
        [
            "log",
            "optimize-tree",
            "baseline",
            "--data-dir",
            str(tmp_path),
            "--tag",
            tag,
            "--commit",
            "deadbeef",
            "--description",
            "baseline",
            "--metric",
            "b=100",
        ]
    )
    # Two macro briefs off the baseline get global brief ids 0 and 1.
    for brief_id, sha, desc in (
        (
            0,
            "aaaaaaa1",
            "round one tries vectorised loads with float four across the inner reduction loop",
        ),
        (
            1,
            "bbbbbbb1",
            "round one tries persistent threadblock cooperation around the vertical stencil window",
        ),
    ):
        _run(
            [
                "log",
                "optimize-tree",
                "brief",
                "--data-dir",
                str(tmp_path),
                "--tag",
                tag,
                "--parent-commit",
                "deadbeef",
                "--brief-kind",
                "macro",
                "--description",
                desc,
            ]
        )
        _run(
            [
                "log",
                "optimize-tree",
                "start",
                "--data-dir",
                str(tmp_path),
                "--tag",
                tag,
                "--brief-id",
                str(brief_id),
            ]
        )
        _run(
            [
                "log",
                "optimize-tree",
                "trial",
                "--data-dir",
                str(tmp_path),
                "--tag",
                tag,
                "--brief-id",
                str(brief_id),
                "--commit",
                sha,
                "--status",
                "succeeded",
                "--description",
                desc + " trial",
                "--metric",
                "b=110",
            ]
        )
